Source: http://www.sunday-times.co.uk/

January 9, 2000
The London Sunday Times

editor@sunday-times.co.uk
http://www.sunday-times.co.uk/
Comment
By Melanie Phillips

BRITAIN IS QUIETLY TURNING INTO A DRUG CULTURE
(MarijuanaNews note: This is amazing and puzzling. As bad as any I have seen. Why would they publish this? The irony is that Britain has long been a " drug culture. " The pub is a social institution.)

It's the nightmare of so many parents with teenage children. The arrest of Nicholas Knatchbull's three friends on suspicion of possessing drugs was the latest in a series of drug incidents concerning Prince William's social circle.
(MarijuanaNews note: A little royal gossip.)

The routine availability of illegal substances is now a fact of life for young people. Keith Hellawell, the " drug tsar ", said last week that drug-taking among well-educated teenagers from stable families was the fastest growing part of the drug racket. Forget cannabis - these kids are going straight for cocaine.

This is a disaster in which the adult world is utterly complicit. The fact that, as Hellawellnoted, middle-class parents are pressuring independent schools to relax their anti-drug rules says it all. Wordly success matters more to them than the health of their young; the use of discipline or law to deter or punish is thought oppressive.

The bottom line is that adults aren't sure whether drugs are a great evil at all. Why, isn't half the professional world snorting lines of cocaine at smart dinner parties?
(MarijuanaNews note: Excuse me, but if " half the professional world snorting lines of cocaine at smart dinner parties " – and they aren’t, they are drinking alcohol - doesn’t that rather suggest that even hard drugs can be used safely by many people.)


This normalisation of illegality merely gives drug-taking added chic for the ever rebellious young. There aren't many issues left, after all, over which the young can rebel. Sex, for so long the revolt of choice, is now reduced to a banal spectator sport for all the family.
(MarijuanaNews note: Sex is a " banal spectator sport for all the family? " That is a bizarre statement, or she has a rather bizarre family.)

Drugs are an easily available source of pleasure. Their catastrophic downside can be easily disregarded by young people whose trademark assumption of invincibility is deepened by the message they've picked up from the adult world that many drugs are no worse than alcohol.
See

The Reality Of the Marijuana Situation In Canada: Unequal Injustice.
Alcohol Costs Canadian Health Almost 100 Times As Much As Marijuana.
Tobacco: Almost 200 As Much – Article and Editorial
and
 " Alcohol abuse exacts $250 billion health care toll. " -- Study.
See If the Media Ignores This One.

The prime minister has said that drugs are the most evil industry confronting modern society. Yet they are tolerated to an astonishing degree. There's zero tolerance of squeegee merchants and neighbours from hell, but zero intolerance of drug use. The police mount all-out campaigns against burglary, domestic violence or racist attacks, but none against drugs. On the contrary, they have effectively decriminalised cannabis and turn a blind eye to other drugs.

Ecstasy, cocaine and cannabis are, after all, an intrinsic part of the club scene. Why aren't the police raiding all such places every night? Maybe they don't because too much is at stake.
(MarijuanaNews note: Or maybe they have more pressing obligations. Or maybe because more and more police think that prohibition is wrong.)

It's hardly an exaggeration to say that some of our inner cities have been regenerated on the back of drug money. The litmus test of a cool British inner city is its night life, which generally means its all-night life, its clubs and dance scene whose sleepless success is oiled by drug-taking. A real war against drugs would close many of these places down.

Yet there's much more than commercial interest behind the official ambivalence towards drugs. Our libertine elites, responsible for creating so many of our social problems, are now intent on creating another. Politicians, police officers, judges, clerics, academics and journalists are flirting openly with legalisation. The implication is that the smartest people think legalisation is the answer, but debate is being prevented by the forces of prejudice.
See
One Writer Knows The Real Reason That UK Politicians Are Afraid Of A Royal Commission:
It Will Say The Same Thing As The Indian Hemp Commission Report Under Queen Victoria.

The greater the hold of drugs on our society, the more the rates of addiction and deaths and car accidents rise, the more calls there are to make drugs legal. This is truly idiotic. It's as if grievous bodily harm, say, had got out of control, and people were urging the legalisation of assault on the basis that all that was really needed was better hospital facilities for the injured and counselling for their attackers.

It's no accident that there's this growing acceptance of drugs legalisation. There's a vast amount of money behind it. George Soros, the billionnaire financier, has invested millions of dollars in influential charities that are pushing legalisation. Soros wants to make most drugs legally available; he says he would first destroy the drug trade by keeping prices low and then would keep raising prices, like taxes on cigarettes, making an exception for registered addicts " to discourage crime ".
(MarijuanaNews note: First, Soros is a prohibitionist. Second, the amount of money given annually to all the anti-prohibitionist organizations in the world would not run the prohibitionist propaganda apparatus for even one day. The ratio really is hundreds to one.)
See
5 Year 2 Billion Dollar Prohibitionist Propaganda Campaign
DEAland Contribution To New UN Prohibitionist Program

This is utter nonsense. Lower prices would attract new customers. Governments would be turned into drug traffickers. Addiction would be institutionalised. Legalisation wouldn't end drug taking; all it would do is take work away from the police and make billions instead for big business.
(MarijuanaNews note: First, no one claims that legalization would end drug taking. Second, " big business " – meaning pharmaceutical companies, the drug testing industry, the payola prohibitionist propaganda media, et al. -- is doing very well under marijuana prohibition. But " big business " could easily be shut out of the " recreational drugs " industry – if that is desirable.)

Yet these insanely dangerous arguments are gaining critical mass. In 1998, an advertisement in The New York Times was signed by hundreds of activists who said - fantastically - that they thought the global war on drugs was " causing more harm than drug abuse itself ", and contrasted " fear, prejudice and punitive prohibitions " with " common sense, science, public health and human rights ".
(MarijuanaNews note: The signatories were not " activists " but very prominent people from around the world.)
See
That Was The Week That -- Wasn’t What the Prohibitionists Planned; The UN " Drug " Summit Farce
The push to create a legal drugs trade rests on two false assertions. The first is that the worst harm done by drugs is through the crime associated with its supply. This completely ignores the death, destruction and social danger produced by the drugs themselves.
See
Survey Of Costs Of Alcohol and " Drug " Abuse
Shows Most of Latter Is From Prohibition;Where Is Marijuana?


The second false claim is that there is such a thing as responsible and safe drug-taking. This belief has taken firm hold in Britain and is behind the shift that has taken place from prevention to " harm reduction ".
(MarijuanaNews note: First, harm reduction does not ignore, much less oppose " prevention. " Second, millions of people in the UK and elsewhere around the world use even a drug as dangerous as alcohol responsibly and safely every day.

That is certainly true of cannabis, which is much less risky than alcohol. She also says that the elites of the UK are using cocaine regularly. That has its risks, but by her own description they don’t seem to be having much trouble with it.)

Clearly, there's a place for harm reduction in treating individual addicts; but the idea that drug-taking can be made safe is utterly wrong. There's no such thing as a harm-free drug. Yet drug " education " is all about telling the young how to take drugs " safely ".
(MarijuanaNews note: Nor is there such a thing as a harm-free law. What the anti-prohibitionists are trying to do is to get the world to look at what the laws are really doing.)
See
How the War On Marijuana To Save The Children
Has Become A War On the Children To Save Marijuana Prohibition

Such classroom materials normalise and encourage drug use, while providing minimal information on harm. They say, for example, that cannabis isn't addictive and is less harmful than tobacco. Yet it is addictive; moreover, cannabis is smoked with tobacco, is itself carcinogenic and, used with tobacco, causes cancer much faster than tobacco alone.
See

Is marijuana addictive?
These materials don't tell young people that hash is more damaging than alcohol. Cannabis hits the immune system. Far from helping multiple sclerosis sufferers, there's evidence that it does them harm.
(MarijuanaNews note: The MS Society of the UK strongly backs medical marijuana use and says that thousands of their members use it. Would they do that if it was making their MS worse? Give them a little credit.)
See
UK To Spend 3 Years And A Million And Half Dollars On Tests
To Find Out If Marijuana Helps MS Patients,
But Will Do No Research To See If Arresting Them Is Harmful.
and
UK Drugs Tsar Claims That Growing Cannabis Strains Without THC
Has Destroyed The Campaign To Legalize Marijuana – There Is No Lie They Will Not Tell.
They don't tell young people that one joint every other day causes permanent brain damage, whereas one point of beer or glass of wine every other day does not.
See
American Journal Of Epidemiology Report That Long-Term Use Of Marijuana
Does Not Lead To A Decline In Mental Function Got Minimal Coverage,
Perhaps Because Scores Actually Fell More Among Non-Users Than Among Heavy Users!
and
David Hadorn Writes: Beyond A Reasonable Doubt Cannabis Is Substantially Less Harmful Than Alcohol Or Tobacco.

They don't tell them that people aren't fit to drive or fly a plane 24 hours after one joint, and that cannabis stays in the blood for weeks.
(MarijuanaNews note: Surely she knows better. The Metabolites of the cannabinoids stay in the body for weeks, not " marijuana " itself. These are not psychoactive.)
See
1994 Dutch Study On " Marijuana Use And Driving " In Real World Conditions
and
Canadian Study Confirms That Marijuana Impairs Driving Far Less Than Alcohol
and links

They don't tell them that, in 1990, the Dutch minister of justice admitted that marijuana-tolerant Holland had become the crime capital of Europe, with a dramatic rise in the use of cannabis, cocaine and opiates.

(MarijuanaNews note: In 1990 the Dutch minister of justice was a prohibitionist, who was subsequently disgraced in a prohibition related scandal, but --in any case -- the statement is both falsie and a non-sequitor. Being tolerant of marijuana has not created crime. In any case, drug use Holland compares favorably in comparison with countries with harsh prohibitionist regimes.)

See
Final Report Of Dutch National Drug Use Survey Will Require New Lies From The Drug Czar:
Their Lifetime Cannabis Use Half of DEAland’s; Two-Thirds That of UK

Or that in Alaska, where cannabis was decriminalised for 10 years, use of hard and soft drugs soared along with crime, and 2,000 people were hospitalised with cannabis-induced psychosis.
(MarijuanaNews note: Nuts! Hard and soft drug use was soaring everywhere during that time. If Alaska, with a population of half a million had 2,000 " hospitalised with cannabis-induced psychosis, " then the rest of the country should have had half a million people " hospitalised with cannabis-induced psychosis. " Didn’t happen. Why didn’t that sound a bit strange to the editors?)

Hard facts, however, have little hope of success against the pull of the pleasure principle and the power of money.

(MarijuanaNews note: Hard facts have little hope of success against the pull of the prohibitionist ideology.)

If this country really wants to wage war on the drug culture, the most effective strategy would be to attack its huge profits by cutting off the money-laundering routes established through secret banking and offshore shell companies.

Would any government though, have the bottle to take on those City financiers who, after a hard day making a fortune out of laundered drug profits, go home to snort a line or two of cocaine with their fashionable friends?

(MarijuanaNews note: This is a bit much. Most " financiers " do not spend there time laundering money, but – again -- if people so successful go home and snort coke, then doesn’t that rather undermine her thesis that " the idea that drug-taking can be made safe is utterly wrong. " )

Melanie Phillips: melaniephillips@msn.com

(MarijuanaNews note: A reader queried Phillips and she provided the following sources for her claims. He was kind enough to forward them to me. I am familiar with most of the studies, and she is not very discriminating, to say the least. Actually, even NIDA would wince at most of them. For example, they never cite Nahas anymore. In any case, there is a huge amount of data that contradicts these claims. There are huge numbers of long term cannabis users, so if the effects were anywhere near as severe as Phillips claims then the hospitals would be full of cannabis users. Kaiser-Permanente did largest long-term study of cannabis users ever and found no major differences in health compared with non-users. The same could not be said of alcohol and tobacco. The Dutch have an excellent public health system and they do not find that cannabis users have any major health problems.

In short, why is it necessary to cite decades old lab studies on monkeys when there is so much empirical data on humans?)


Sources cited by Phillips

" Physical and psychological addiction [Compton; Kaplan, Kaufman; Miller; Schwartz]

Half of daily users estimated to become dependent [Anthony and Helger]
Long term brain damage: memory and complex brain functions affected for weeks after use [Schwartz; Solowij]
Abnormal changes in brain cells, brain blood flow and brain wave patterns [Lex; Mathew; Nahas; Devane]
Serious and persistent brain damage in monkeys made to smoke equivalent of 1.5 joints per day for 6 months [Heath; McGahan]
(MarijuanaNews note: The Heath monkey study dates back to the early 1970s and was criticized at the time for both the dosage and the means of testing, wires in the monkeys’ brains.)
Brain cells permanently lose ability to function; brain wave studies of occasional marijuana smokers among students showed 40-50% decrease in brain energy [Nahas; Gilkeson]
(MarijuanaNews note: Gilkeson may be even worse than Nahas.)

Chronic use leads to prefrontal lobe dysfunction in the brain and changed identity, harming reasoning and the ability to distinguish fact from fiction and creating feelings of being lonely, bored and misunderstood [Lundqvist and Ericsson]
Among young users, early signs of lung cancer development associated with elderly tobacco smokers [Tashkin; Taylor; Tennant]
Increased risk of leukaemia to children [Robison, Buckley, Daigle et al]
(MarijuanaNews note: This study was on a very small sample, depended on self-reporting, and there has been no change in the instance of that type of leukemia over decades.)
Many other abnormalities in unborn children including lower IQ [Quasi, Mariano, Milman; Ward; Hatch and Bracken; Day; others]
Short term memory impairment [Schwartz, Grunewald, Klitzner and Fedio; many others]
Measurable learning deficits in occasional users [Kamine, Behaviour of Pharmacology]
Heavy cannabis users (20 joints or more per month) had slow reactions, disability in personal social and vocational areas and neurotic and psychotic behaviour [Varma, Drug and Alcohol Dependence]
Hallucinosis, depersonalisation and paranoia as well as development of psychoses [Solomons; Voth and Schwartz]
Damage to immune system [Diaz; Cusher; Watzl; others]
Decline in sperm count [New England Journal of Medicine]
Two marijuana cigarettes a day as harmful to lungs as 28 of tobacco [Starr]
Murderers claim they killed while under influence of marijuana [International Journal of the Addictions]
Increase in aggression among inner city males [Cherek, Psychopharmacology]
Panic, paranoia, fear of dying, loss of time sense, anxiety, tension and confusion from higher doses [Klonoff]

Risk factor for schizophrenia [Allebleck; Jablensky]
In some cases effects mirror effects of senility [Sulkowski].
There are many other studies. "

(MarijuanaNews note: So many studies, so few bodies.)
